concepts.title: Octet Rule, Ionic and Electrovalent Bonding
concepts.definition: Atoms combine to complete their octet through ionic bonds where electrons transfer from metals to non-metals forming cations and anions held by electrostatic attraction, and lattice enthalpy decides the stability of ionic compounds.
concepts.key_idea: Ionic compounds are crystalline solids with high melting points, soluble in polar solvents and conductors in molten or solution state.
concepts.textbook_ref: kech104.txt octet rule and ionic bonding sections

concepts.title: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures and Valence Bond Approach
concepts.definition: A covalent bond forms by sharing of electron pairs between atoms, Lewis structures show bonding and lone pairs, and the valence bond theory explains bond formation by overlap of half filled orbitals with directional character producing sigma and pi bonds.
concepts.key_idea: Sigma bonds arise from axial overlap while pi bonds come from sidewise overlap, and coordinate bonds form when both electrons come from one atom.

concepts.title: Hybridisation, VSEPR and Molecular Geometry
concepts.definition: Hybridisation mixes atomic orbitals of comparable energy into equivalent hybrids like sp, sp2, sp3, and the VSEPR theory predicts molecular geometry from electron pair repulsions, with lone pair lone pair repulsion exceeding lone pair bond pair repulsion.
concepts.key_idea: Shapes follow from the number of electron domains: linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal and octahedral for two to six domains.

concepts.title: Molecular Orbital Theory and Bond Order Computation
concepts.definition: Molecular orbital theory forms bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals by linear combination of atomic orbitals, electrons fill them in increasing energy, and the bond order equals half the difference between the number of electrons in bonding and antibonding orbitals, deciding stability and magnetic behaviour.
concepts.key_idea: A positive bond order means the molecule exists; paramagnetism appears when unpaired electrons occupy orbitals, as in dioxygen.
